title: Constructibility of geometric connected-component-count level sets
statement: Let $f:Y\to T$ be a morphism of finite presentation of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For $t\in T$, let $n_f(t)\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ be the well-defined geometric connected-component count of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change]: the number of maximal nonempty connected subsets of $Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}K$ for any algebraically closed extension $K$ of the residue field $\kappa(t)$, with an infinite number recorded as $\infty$ and the empty fibre having count $0$. For each integer $m\geq0$, put $E_m(f)=\{t\in T:n_f(t)=m\}$. Then $E_m(f)$ is locally constructible: every point of $T$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ such that $E_m(f)\cap V$ is constructible in $V$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. If $T$ is Noetherian, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], $E_m(f)$ is constructible in $T$. No smoothness, properness, flatness, section, normality or nonemptiness hypothesis on $Y$ or $T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 055I, label lemma-nr-geom-connected-components-constructible, all finite level sets E_m; its proof explicitly proves constructibility for Noetherian T. The geometric component count is the already-existing node lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change.

proof.text: First assume $T$ is Noetherian. By [pqf-def-locnoeth], local Noetherianity supplies an affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings; quasi-compactness supplies a finite subcover, as required by [lem-trf-noetherian-constructible-subset-criterion]. Finite presentation implies finite type: its affine algebras have finitely many generators, and the morphism is quasi-compact [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each nonempty irreducible closed $Z\subseteq|T|$, apply [lem-sfb-geometric-connected-count-generic-constancy] to obtain a nonempty relatively open $W\subseteq Z$ and a constant value $c$ of $n_f$ on $W$. If $c=m$, then $W\subseteq E_m(f)$; otherwise $W\cap E_m(f)=\varnothing$. Thus [lem-trf-noetherian-constructible-subset-criterion] proves that $E_m(f)$ is constructible in $T$. This proves the global Noetherian clause.

source.place: Tag 055I, label lemma-nr-geom-connected-components-constructible; second paragraph: apply 053Z and 055H.

proof.text: For arbitrary $T$ and $t\in T$, choose an affine open neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $t$, and let $f_V:Y\times_TV\to V$ be the restriction. It is of finite presentation by the base-change clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The count identity of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change] for the open immersion $V\to T$ gives $E_m(f_V)=E_m(f)\cap V$. It suffices to prove constructibility of this subset in $V$.

source.place: Tag 055I, label lemma-nr-geom-connected-components-constructible; first paragraph: reduce to an affine neighbourhood.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine] to $V$: the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $A_i\subseteq A$ give a small cofiltered affine-transition system $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with limit $V$. Each $V_i$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since it is of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-family-descent] to the singleton family $f_V$ to obtain an index $i$, a finitely presented $f_i:Y_i\to V_i$, and a cartesian square identifying $f_V$ with its base change along $a:V\to V_i$. All stages satisfy the qcqs hypothesis of this descent theorem.

source.place: Tag 055I, label lemma-nr-geom-connected-components-constructible; first paragraph: affine Noetherian approximation and 01ZM(1).

proof.text: Apply step 1 to $f_i$ over its Noetherian base $V_i$; hence $E_m(f_i)$ is constructible. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change], $n_{f_V}(v)=n_{f_i}(a(v))$ for every $v\in V$, so $E_m(f_V)=a^{-1}(E_m(f_i))$. By [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage] this inverse image is constructible in $V$. Step 2 identifies it with $E_m(f)\cap V$. This gives the required neighbourhood for every $t$, proving local constructibility. The count identities and the dichotomy in step 1 include $m=0$ and empty fibres.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q95-d793fac09 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 055I (lemma-nr-geom-connected-components-constructible), 055H (lemma-nr-geom-connected-components-good) and 054I in full. The item's statement, unchanged from live, matches 055I, including the Noetherian global clause that 055I's second paragraph proves. The four steps follow 055I in order. Step 1 applies the 053Z criterion with the new 055H node, after checking the finite Noetherian cover, finite presentation implying finite type, the c=m dichotomy and that irreducible sets are nonempty. Step 2 localises to an affine open using clause (3) of qcqs-permanence and the 055F count base change. Step 3 uses Nagata affine approximation, affine-qcqs, finite type over Z being Noetherian, and 01ZM(1) singleton descent, whose hypotheses I checked. Step 4 uses 055F along a:V->V_i and the 054I preimage leaf. The new node lem-sfb-geometric-connected-count-generic-constancy is 055H restated for irreducible closed Z, which is equivalent in a scheme because every such Z has a generic point. It is statement-only, self-contained, has real searches recorded and no Mathlib match, and is strictly smaller than the item, so it is not a restatement. It duplicates no existing node: 055A trf is about irreducible counts, 055G sbc covers only c=1, and the 0554 lower bound is about irreducible components. I searched the snapshot, live and side-live. I tested small cases: V(x(x-t)) over A^1, the empty Y, D(t) into A^1, and two crossing lines. Batch-5 finding: lem-trf-noetherian-constructible-subset-criterion is the generic topology fact 053Z. Its closure contains no other trace-formula, Poincaré or nt node, and it is not part of either assumed statement or its proof, so I accept it. I accept the declared tool_uses as generic 055I tools. There are no SGA citations, the item is not superseded on live, and I made no fixes.

lean.statement: theorem isLocallyConstructible_geometricConnectedComponentCount_levelSet {Y T : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (m : ℕ) : Topology.IsLocallyConstructible {t : T | ENat.card (ConnectedComponents (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) (AlgebraicClosure (T.residueField t)))) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t) : Scheme.{u})) = (m : ℕ∞)} ∧ (IsNoetherian T → Topology.IsConstructible {t : T | ENat.card (ConnectedComponents (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) (AlgebraicClosure (T.residueField t)))) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t) : Scheme.{u})) = (m : ℕ∞)})
